items.title: [Feat] serving: Add --clamp-max-new-tokens-to-context to cap max_tokens when the prompt fits
items.author: Alex-Wengg
items.summary: When the prompt fits the context but prompt + does not, returns 400. Clients often cannot compute the exact prompt length (it depends on the server's tokenizer and chat template), so a client that sends a fixed cap, or computes one from an estimated prompt len…
items.body:
## Motivation

Closes #45841.

When the prompt fits the context but prompt + `max_new_tokens` does not, `TokenizerManager._validate_one_request` returns 400. Clients often cannot compute the exact prompt length (it depends on the server's tokenizer and chat template), so a client that sends a fixed `max_tokens` cap, or computes one from an estimated prompt length, gets rejected. The OpenAI API defines `max_tokens` / `max_completion_tokens` as an upper bound, and the scheduler already treats it that way: `init_req_max_new_tokens` clamps it to `max_req_len - input_len - 1` and to the KV budget.

items.title: [diffusion] Breakable CUDA graphs on by default for LTX-2/LTX-2.3 two-stage serving
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Enables breakable CUDA graphs by default for LTX-2/LTX-2.3 two-stage diffusion serving, reducing latency 20-44% while maintaining bitwise-equal output.
items.body:
## Motivation

LTX-2 two-stage stage 1 runs at half resolution (~1.5k video tokens), so its step is launch-bound: on 4xB300, TRT-LLM's CUDA-graph configuration runs a stage-1 step in 0.044 s against 0.192 s for sglang eager. Breakable CUDA graphs (BCG) close most of that gap, and the graphs replay the same kernels, so the output is bitwise equal to eager. Today BCG is opt-in, so every flagless LTX deployment leaves this on the table.

BCG stays opt-in everywhere else. The validated-model list records correctness, not speed: FLUX.3 won 1 of 10 cells, Qwen-Image-2.1 on 1 GPU is 0.5% slower, and

Every LTX-2 denoising step pays two host-side costs.

items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Under, dynamo guards on that dict's size. DiT blocks share one compiled forward, so every new linear a block brings changes the size and recompiles the frame.
items.body:
## Motivation

#44643 caches the fused linear-GELU verdict per linear in a module-level `WeakKeyDictionary`, `_VERDICTS`. Under `torch.compile`, dynamo guards on that dict's size. items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Fixes dynamic LoRA adapter weights being silently dropped when fused linear-GELU epilogue reads only the base layer's.weight/.bias, bypassing the LoRA wrapper.
items.body:
## Motivation

`FUSED_LINEAR_GELU` is in the `"lossless"` tier, and `quality` has defaulted to `"lossless"` since #42370, so the fused linear+GELU epilogue mounts by default. With a dynamic (unmerged) LoRA, the site's linear is a `BaseLayerWithLoRA`. Its `.weight` and `.bias` forward to the base layer, and it passed every duck-typed guard. So `fused_linear_gelu_tanh(x, proj_in.weight, proj_in.bias)` multiplied the base weight only and silently dropped the adapter's delta.

This affects every GELU site that serves a dynamic LoRA:
- LTX-2 two-stage, stage 2, always: the distilled LoRA is applied

items.title: [Fix] diffusion/ltx: Keep tiled VAE decode off the sharded convs under parallel decode
items.author: mickqian
items.summary: Fixes corrupted VAE tile boundaries in LTX diffusion models by bypassing sharded convolutions during tiled parallel decode, reducing max pixel error from 135 levels to near noise floor.
items.body:
## Motivation

With more than one decode rank (CFG parallel, TP or SP), the LTX VAE installs spatially sharded convs that exchange halo rows with the neighbouring rank. Those convs expect each rank to hold its own height split. But:
- `_decode` checked tiling before the sharded path;
- `tiled_decode`, `_temporal_tiled_decode` and `decode_chunk` called the decoder on whole tensors while the sharded convs were installed.

So each rank blended its neighbour's copy of the same tile into its own edge rows.

Decoding a real LTX-2 latent (768x512x121) on 2xH200, with 2 decode ranks compared against 1

items.title: [Perf] dsv4: Optionally stage V4.1 engram rows from the shared host table on the scheduler
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Adds opt-in engram row staging that pre-fetches DSV4.1 rows to GPU on a side stream during scheduling, avoiding PCIe bandwidth bottlenecks on non-ATS GPUs.

On GPUs without ATS, the GPU maps the shared Engram host table in its own page tables. A gather of random rows from a table far larger than its translation reach then runs at a fraction of PCIe bandwidth, and it sits on the forward stream. Sorted reads soften this but do not remove it.

items.title: [Perf] dsv4: Drop local references that keep residual-stream tensors alive through the prefill step
items.author: hnyls2002
items.summary: Drops early local references to residual-stream tensors in DeepSeek-V4 prefill, reducing peak memory and eliminating allocator retries at large batch sizes without changing computation.
items.body:
- In `DeepseekV4Model`, three local names kept a full residual-stream tensor alive longer than needed during a prefill step:

items.title: [Bugfix][KV Offload][P2P] Close P2P DEALERs with LINGER 0
items.author: vMaroon
items.summary: Fixes P2P control plane deadlock caused by infinite LINGER on DEALER sockets, which blocks libzmq I/O threads when queued messages can't be delivered to stalled peers.
items.body:
## Overview

`ZmqConnection.close()` closes the session DEALER with the default infinite `LINGER`. When the peer stopped answering with a message still queued, that DEALER outlives `close()` and keeps reconnecting, and its monitor events, whose reader is already closed, block libzmq's I/O thread. Every P2P control socket in the engine then stops until restart, so P2P lookups to all peers wait out their 30 s deadline before falling back to local prefill. This closes the DEALER with `linger=0`, as `ZmqTransport.close()` already does for the ROUTER and the context.

items.author: Hrithvik-Alex
items.summary: With (#40453), GPU memory after weight loading is higher than with the default loader, and the KV cache shrinks by the difference. On GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4 on B200, "Load weight end" mem usage was 108.89 GB against 106.88 GB for the default loader.
items.body:
## Motivation

With `--load-format instanttensor` (#40453), GPU memory after weight loading is higher than with the default loader, and the KV cache shrinks by the difference. On GLM-5.3 NVFP4, TP4 on B200, "Load weight end" mem usage was 108.89 GB against 106.88 GB for the default loader. That cost 812k KV tokens against 836k.

There are two causes:

1. **A lazily created NCCL communicator.** InstantTensor all-gathers over `get_parallel().world_group.device_group`. SGLang never otherwise runs a collective on that group (its world-group uses are CPU-group object collectives and barriers)

items.summary: The Rust server currently drops a request's W3C trace context: api.v1 has no field for it, and the scheduler header always sends. So emits no per-request spans and SGLang's scheduler will be excluded from any tracing.

## Motivation

The Rust server currently drops a request's W3C trace context: api.v1 has no field for it, and the scheduler header always sends `time_stats=nil`. So `--enable-trace` emits no per-request spans and SGLang's scheduler will be excluded from any tracing.

The legacy `sglang.runtime.v1` path had carried this context (`GenerateRequest.trace_headers`).

## Modifications

- api.v1 `GenerateRequest` gains `map<string, string> external_trace_header = 33`, named after `GenerateReqInput`'s field. Rust HTTP `/generate` and gRPC `Generate` both honor it.

items.body:
## Description

In adaptive mode, the MiniMax-M3 chat template ends the prompt at the assistant header without prefilling `<mm:think>` or `</mm:think>`, and the model emits its own tags. The server resolves the reasoning mode from the end of the rendered prompt, but returned nothing for such a prompt, so the request's own `enable_thinking` reached `MiniMaxM3ReasoningParser`. The template never reads that key. The Anthropic adapter sets it for `thinking: {"type": "enabled"}`, so the parser prepended `<mm:think>` to output that already opened with one, and the tag leaked into the thinking block.

items.title: [Bug] FP4 KV block scales are dropped by PD transfer and cpu_tensor retraction (fp4_mx_block16 gives garbage)
items.author: wenhug
items.summary: Decode then dequantizes with whatever scales are sitting in its own pool: zeros on a fresh pool, someone else's later on. Decode retraction with has the same issue.
items.body:
### Describe the bug

With FP4 KV cache (`--kv-cache-dtype fp4_mx_block16`), PD disaggregation sends the packed KV but not the block scales. Decode then dequantizes with whatever scales are sitting in its own pool: zeros on a fresh pool, someone else's later on. Output is garbage. Decode retraction with `cpu_tensor` has the same issue.

- PD: `setup_state_kv_args` only registers `BLOCK_SCALE` for `MHATokenToKVPoolMXFP8`. FP4 pools are a plain `MHATokenToKVPool` with a quant method, so their `k_scale_buffer` / `v_scale_buffer` never get registered.
- Retraction: `MHATokenToKVPool.get_cpu_copy`

## Overview

On GB10 (DGX Spark, sm_121), cuBLAS runs a **one-row** BF16 lm_head (`x[1, K] @ W[V, K]^T`) as a GEMV that reads the weight at ~175 GB/s. items.title: [Bugfix] shm_broadcast: poll the notify socket from busy readers
items.author: ZJY0516
items.summary: Fixes unbounded memory growth in SHM broadcast readers that never poll their CONFLATE notify socket, causing libzmq command backlog to accumulate under sustained distributed inference load.
items.body:
## Overview

Fixes #63026. A local SHM reader that keeps reading (which is the normal state under load) never touches its `CONFLATE` notify socket, and libzmq queues an internal command for every write notification until it does. Reader memory then grows with every message. This PR polls the notify socket from `SpinCondition.record_read()` at most once per second.

## Claims

- Reader-side memory stays bounded under sustained load. Before this change, every message added ~41 B to the reader's libzmq mailbox. That affects each worker's RPC broadcast reader (2 messages per step) and EngineCore

items.author: cjackal
items.summary: With, chat streaming counts reasoning tokens over the whole output after every delta. For engine-based reasoning parsers, when the prompt already closes reasoning (thinking disabled or ), each of those counts re-decodes and re-parses the entire output.
items.body:
## Overview



With `stream_options.continuous_usage_stats=true`, chat streaming counts reasoning tokens over the whole output after every delta. For engine-based reasoning parsers, when the prompt already closes reasoning (thinking disabled or `continue_final_message`), each of those counts re-decodes and re-parses the entire output. That makes per-delta frontend cost linear and total cost quadratic in output length. This PR makes that count incremental.

This matters in production because gateways and routers often force `continuous_usage_stats` on every stream, for per-request tok

## Motivation

**What goes wrong**
With `ENABLE_CK=0`, `AITerImpl.forward` calls `aiter.flash_attn_func` inside `torch.compile`. That dispatch opens a Triton config JSON and builds a Triton kernel Dynamo cannot reconstruct. The graph break is inside the DiT block loop, so Dynamo skips `Flux2Transformer2DModel.forward` on the first real step.

**Where it shows up**
gfx1250 already takes `AITerImpl._forward_bf16_eager`, which is `@torch.compiler.disable`, because FlyDSL's Python JIT is not traceable. gfx950 with CK enabled stays on `FlashAttnFunc` and is unchanged. The failure shows up on MI355

items.summary: Split out from the Ling-3.1-flash day-0 support effort. Block-FP8 decode on Hopper spends small-M linear work in GEMM kernels that are built for large batches, the KDA output normalization and FP8 quantization run as separate kernels, the 512-expert sigmoid ro…
items.body:
## Motivation

Split out from the Ling-3.1-flash day-0 support effort.

Block-FP8 decode on Hopper spends small-M linear work in GEMM kernels that are built for large batches, the KDA output normalization and FP8 quantization run as separate kernels, the 512-expert sigmoid router goes through a generic Triton top-k, and weights whose K dimension is not a multiple of the 128-wide quantization block cannot use the native Triton/DeepGEMM paths at all. This PR adds opt-in fast paths for each, with explicit dispatch contracts and no change to default behavior.

Measured on H200 with Ling-3.1-flash

items.author: zheyuf

items.body:
## Description

After the indexer scores a MiniMax-M3 context chunk, each (token, index head) row picks its 16 highest-scoring 128-token blocks. `minimax_m3_select_blocks` reads each row on its own, strided by the token count, because the scores are stored token-contiguous. For an 8k-token chunk over a 139k-token context, with 4 index heads per rank as on the attention-DP prefill worker, it takes 480 us per layer on B300, about as long as scoring the chunk.

items.author: Pepsi-Cola-qqq
items.summary: Catches exceptions during lazy batch_lookup iteration in AsyncLookupManager, resolving failed request groups as misses instead of aborting the entire batch and stalling workers.
items.body:
## Overview

Catch errors raised while *consuming* the `batch_lookup` iterator in tiering `AsyncLookupManager`, so a lazy backend failure resolves the request group as misses instead of losing the whole batch and stalling worker progress. Follows the issue addressed by closed, unmerged PR #59187.

## Claims

- An exception raised mid-iteration of `batch_lookup` (not just on the initial call) now resolves that request group as misses instead of dropping the batch.
- Healthy request groups in the same batch, and subsequent batches, keep making progress.
- Regression tests cover both a failure

items.author: LopezCastroRoberto
items.summary: Fix illegal shared-memory write in cooperative_topk caused by nvcc compiling integer bitwise-OR as FP negation, producing wrong NaN ordering when top-k rows exceed the threshold.
items.body:
## Purpose

Since #59645, `cooperative_topk` crashes with `cudaErrorIllegalAddress` when a row of 64K columns or more contains more NaNs than `top_k` (e.g. 1% of a 256K row, or a fully-NaN row). NaN scores can reach decode top-k during warmup and CUDA-graph capture, where the indexer reads uninitialized KV blocks (see the note in `candidate_blocks.py`). Before #59645 such rows produced garbage indices; now they take down the process.

**Root cause.** nvcc compiles the integer expression `bits | 0x80000000u` in `convert_to_uint32_v2` as the FP operation `-|x|`:

```

items.title: [Bugfix][Pooling] Validate late-interaction mode and use count in the Python API
items.author: he-yufeng
items.summary: Adds input validation to LateInteractionParams so invalid mode strings and non-positive use counts raise errors upfront instead of silently producing wrong pooler output or crashing at runtime.
items.body:
## Overview

`LateInteractionParams` had no validation, and bad inputs fail in the worst places:

- An unknown `mode` string is silently skipped by the late-interaction runner (`_parse_late_interaction_meta` returns `None` for anything outside `cache_query`/`score_doc`), so a typo produces ordinary pooler output instead of an error.
- `cache_query` with `query_uses=None` crashes on the runner's `assert query_uses is not None`.
- `query_uses <= 0` poisons the cache lifecycle: the entry pops on the first `score_doc`, so the remaining paired documents fail with a cache miss.

`__post_init__` now

## Purpose

raises `ValueError`, although common multiples 10 and 20 exist.

Use `math.lcm()` and retain the existing rounding and size-limit behavior.
The regression covers coprime widths, divisible widths, and disabled sequence
parallelism without silently changing `enable_sp`.

items.title: [Bugfix][Core] Set TRITON_CACHE_DIR at worker startup to stop Triton kernels rebuilding on every start
items.author: menglcai
items.summary: Fixes Triton kernel cache being written outside VLLM_CACHE_ROOT, causing unnecessary rebuilds on restart by explicitly setting TRITON_CACHE_DIR at worker startup.
items.body:
## Overview

vLLM now sets `TRITON_CACHE_DIR` when a worker starts. Without it, Triton writes vLLM's own `@triton.jit` kernels to `~/.triton/cache`, which is outside `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT`. A deployment that preserves only the vLLM cache therefore rebuilds those kernels at every start, even when the AOT compile cache hits.

## Claims

- A server that starts with a populated `VLLM_CACHE_ROOT` no longer rebuilds vLLM's hand-written Triton kernels.
- On a gfx1151 deployment, the start time drops from 127 s to 51 s.
- The model outputs do not change, and the steady-state throughput does not change.

items.body:
<!-- markdownlint-disable -->

## Overview

This PR ports the deferred spec decode state of #61434 (Qwen3.8 GDN) to the GLM-5.3-Flash KDA recurrent kernel on ROCm.

Today a spec decode step stores the full fp32 state after every draft token, but the next step reads only the state at the last accepted token. With this PR the kernel:
- stores the full state only after token 0;
- records each later token's inputs in its own slot;
- replays the accepted records at the start of the next step.

Related:
- #61434: the GDN version.
- #61761: DFlash2 performance on ROCm.
- #63073: a faster Gluon kernel

items.body:

## Overview

GLM-5.3-Flash cannot be compiled with torch.compile. On ROCm, the default FULL_AND_PIECEWISE mode therefore falls back to FULL_DECODE_ONLY, and every prefill or mixed prefill+decode step runs eagerly.

items.title: [Bugfix][ROCm] Use 64-bit row offsets in the Triton W4A16 GEMM
items.author: subin9
items.summary: Fixes ROCm crashes in the W4A16 Triton GEMM kernel caused by int32 row-offset overflow when M×K or M×N exceeds 2^31.
items.body:
## Purpose

Fixes #63049. `triton_w4a16_gemm_kernel` indexes activations and outputs with int32 row offsets, which wrap once M × K or M × N passes 2^31 and fault on ROCm. Casting `pid_m` to int64 makes both products 64-bit. The weight, scale and zero-point offsets do not depend on M and stay int32.

## Test Plan

The new test runs the GEMM one block of rows past each bound, (K, N) = (256, 34816) for the output offsets and (17408, 256) for the activation offsets, and compares the last 64 rows with the float32 reference already in the file.

I also called `_triton_w4a16_gemm_impl` alone at a Qwe

items.author: leslie-fang25
items.summary: Fixes a flaky NVFP4 gather act-fusion test caused by E4M3 rounding-midpoint mismatches between fp32 kernel and bf16-rounded reference, adjusting test thresholds accordingly.
items.body:
The kernel computes the activation and per-block amax in fp32, while the reference rounds the GEMM output and the Relu2 output to bf16 before fp4_quantize. Blocks whose scale factor sits near an E4M3 rounding midpoint then round to the adjacent code, which affects 2-5% of the blocks for Relu2, so the 95% exact-match threshold failed intermittently (~2.6% of runs for 8192-8-1-128-relu2).

Verified locally on GB300 and B200 by repeating each case with fresh random inputs (failures / runs)

  | Case (relu2) | With fix, GB300 | With fix, B200 | Without fix, GB300 | Without fix, B200 |
  |---|

items.body:
# MegaMoE Support Status and Roadmap
This Roadmap is based on the [dev branch](https://github.com/NVIDIA/Megatron-LM/tree/dev)

## 1 MegaMoE Overview

## Description

Author: @zheyuf (moved from GitLab by @Tabrizian).

Muse Spark Open's DFlash2 drafters could only run on the VANILLA attention backend. This PR lets them run on TRTLLM and makes that the default.

Why: VANILLA keeps the drafter's KV in its own buffer outside the KV cache manager. items.title: Batch-invariant ordered TP reductions for TP>=3
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: For a given element, NCCL's summation order depends on where that element sits in the message (ring rotation, chunking, and the algorithm it picks for the message size). The training forward ( rows) and the inference engine (flat decode rows) place the same to…
items.body:
## Problem

Under `batch_invariant_mode`, tensor-parallel forward reductions at TP >= 3 are not batch-invariant. For a given element, NCCL's summation order depends on where that element sits in the message (ring rotation, chunking, and the algorithm it picks for the message size). The training forward (`[s, b]` rows) and the inference engine (flat decode rows) place the same token at different positions, so they get different bits for that token. Measured on Ultra-L8 TP4xEP4 with the stock reduce: 576/576 tokens differed (max 1.3e-2). With the ordered reduce, all 576/576 were bitwise equal.

Fix the generic torch fused forward path for FSDP2-managed LM heads,
including models such as Qwen3.

Previously, the fused forward accessed `lm_head.weight` directly,
bypassing the LM head's FSDP2 hooks and potentially mixing regular
Tensors with DTensors during matrix multiplication.

This change installs a fused LM head forward during backend initialization
and runs fused computation through `self.lm_head(...)`. It preserves
torch/liger backend selection and handles DTensor weights, device placement,
and hidden-state dtype inside the module boundary.

items.author: 0z5a
items.summary: stops after its first profile when shuts down the Nsight session and terminates the torchrun launcher. The launcher exits with a signal error, so prevents the nondeterministic profile and comparison from running.
items.body:
`run_nsys_breakdown.sh` stops after its first profile when `cudaProfilerStop()` shuts down the Nsight session and terminates the torchrun launcher. The launcher exits with a signal error, so `set -e` prevents the nondeterministic profile and comparison from running.

Use `--capture-range-end=stop` to stop collection while allowing the target application to finish its cleanup and exit normally. The entry point is still responsible for having a finite run; the profiling window remains bounded by the CUDA profiler API.

Validation on a single GH200 (aarch64), Nsight Systems 2025.6.3.541, PyTorch

items.summary: Proposes shared-prefix packing for FSDP to eliminate redundant prompt computation across GRPO rollout samples, achieving up to 3.8x speedup with no memory increase.
items.body:
## 1. Summary

In GRPO-style RL in verl every prompt is sampled `rollout.n` times, so the actor, reference and critic each run a forward pass over every (prompt, response) pair and process the same prompt `n` times per group. This RFC adds **shared-prefix packing to the FSDP engine**, where the `n` samples of a prompt are packed as one trunk (the prompt) plus one branch per response. items.author: zheyuf
items.summary: With TP, every rank reads the whole index-K cache in every decode step, although it only scores its own index heads. At long contexts that read dominates the index scorer.
items.body:
## Description

With TP, every rank reads the whole index-K cache in every decode step, although it only scores its own index heads. At long contexts that read dominates the index scorer.

`sparse_attention_config.index_tp_split` (off by default) splits that read: each rank reads 1/TP of the index-K rows, scores all index heads on them, and writes its per-block maxima straight into the owning rank's memory over CUDA IPC. bump when a prompt reaches a terminal status. On 8x MI355X GSM8K GRPO it cuts `timing_s/gen` by 22–31%

items.title: Fix YaRN cache reuse for shorter context-parallel sequences
items.author: Sunt-ing
items.summary: With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks.
items.body:
- [X] I, the PR author, have personally reviewed every line of this PR.

# What does this PR do?

With context parallelism, running a shorter sequence after a longer one can reuse the wrong YaRN positions and change the model's output. The cache contains positions already split between CP ranks. For CP2 rank 0, length 64 caches positions `0…15, 48…63`, but length 32 needs `0…7, 24…31`. Taking a prefix of the old cache gives the wrong positions.

Rebuild the cache when a non-packed sequence shrinks with CP > 1. CP1 and packed inputs can still reuse the cache.

…he actor and reference model

vLLM never samples some token ids (the out-of-tokenizer tail, plus the vision placeholders): it sets their logits to -inf before sampling. The actor and the reference model still compute probabilities over the full vocabulary, so the policy that is sampled from and the policy being trained differ. Nothing in training then keeps the actor's probability on those ids in check, and it can drift freely since they are never sampled and never penalized.

items.author: shjwudp

items.body:

Add opt-in `SchedulePolicy(reduce_scatter_interval=k)` to MFSDP v2. A module reuses one full local-gradient buffer per trainable parameter group, accumulates in main-gradient precision, and reduces every `k` completed backwards. Fixes #7857.

## What

`TorchSampling.filter_logits` ran `last_token_logits.div_(temperature)` in
the input's dtype. For BF16/FP16 logits that

  - loses precision in the scaled logit and shifts top-p nucleus membership
    at moderate temperatures like 0.1, and
  - overflows FP16 at temperature=0 (the divisor is floored to
    `MIN_SAMPLING_TEMPERATURE=1e-6` → `logits * 1e6` → `inf`).

Issue #7857 documents both failures on a trained Nemotron-H-8B-Base-8K through
the dynamic engine: BF16 rounding changes which token wins at temperature=0.1,
top_p=0.9; FP16 scaling overflows at temperature=0.

`experimental_fn` / `experimental_cls` decide whether an experimental API has reached its end of life by comparing only the *minor* component of the version:

PkgVersion(introduced_with_version).minor + max_lifetime < PkgVersion(mcore_version).minor
```

items.body:
### What does this PR do?

Rollout routing replay (R3) returns one routed-experts row per token vLLM ran. The agent loop places those rows on the trainer's prompt by position. Nothing checks that the two prompts are the same token sequence.

They can differ for multimodal prompts. vLLM's multimodal processor expands each image placeholder into a span, so the prompt vLLM runs can be longer than the prompt the trainer replays on. items.title: [perf] Long prompts are slow to preprocess with the pinned Transformers version
items.author: lbaolin
items.summary: Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost even when they contain only text. Hugging Face already fixed this in huggingface/transformers#47580, released in Transformers 5.15.0.
items.body:
### Problem

veRL pins Transformers 5.12.1, which has a slow CPU check for image/video special tokens. Long prompts sent through a multimodal processor pay this cost **even when they contain only text**.

Hugging Face already fixed this in huggingface/transformers#47580, released in Transformers 5.15.0. veRL's default dependencies still select the older version.

### Measured result

Using veRL's processor helper with the public Qwen3.5-2B processor and a 131,084-token synthetic prompt:

| Configuration | Time per processor call |
| --- | --- |
| Transformers 5.12.1, current default | 1.58 s |

items.title: [MoE] Opt-in EP-size-invariant expert combine (fixed fp32 reduction tree)
items.author: wdykas
items.summary: Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout.
items.body:
**Problem.** Under `batch_invariant_mode`, the MoE combine sums each token's local expert outputs per EP rank, rounds that partial to fp32, and then adds the rank partials in rank order. Where the fp32 roundings fall therefore depends on the expert-parallel size. The same token gets different bits at EP 1, 2 and 4, so batch-invariant training and inference only agree when both use the same EP layout. That rules out, for example, training at EP8 while generating at EP4.

Measured on Nemotron-3-Nano (top-6, hidden 2688) in our RL setup, which uses the same combine:
- One MoE layer at EP2 vs EP1

### What does this PR do?

Honor `inference.temperature` when computing vLLM teacher prompt logprobs for on-policy distillation.

Previously, teacher prompt logprobs were computed at T=1 even when the configured temperature differed. This could produce a temperature mismatch between teacher targets and student training probabilities.

This PR applies `log_softmax(teacher_logits / T)` before extracting observed-token and top-k logprobs. The existing configuration inherits the student rollout temperature by default, so both use the same T without adding a new option.

Fixes #7769.

items.summary: This coupled every submodule of (e.g.,, ) to the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need synchronous rule-based reward functions. [Discussion: Thanks for the review!]
items.body:
## Background

`vime.rollout.rm_hub.__init__` imported `aiohttp` at module load time. This
coupled every submodule of `rm_hub` (e.g. `math_utils`, `f1`, `gpqa`) to
the full async remote-reward runtime, even though most callers only need
synchronous rule-based reward functions.

## Problem

Running reward CPU tests in a lightweight contributor environment fails
during pytest collection, before any test body executes:

```
tests/test_rm_math.py:21: in <module>
    from vime.rollout.rm_hub.math_utils import (...)
vime/rollout/rm_hub/__init__.py:5: in <module>
    import aiohttp
E   ModuleNotFound
discussion:
Thanks for the review! I have added a `TYPE_CHECKING` block that imports `aiohttp` for static type checkers while preserving the lazy import behavior at runtime:

```python
from typing import TYPE_CHECKING
...
if TYPE_CHECKING:
    import a

items.body:
Ouro's deep loops can be grouped across response positions instead of running
them immediately after every shallow readout. This adds an inference-only runner
that retains loop-two states, batches loops three and four at a fixed deep-readout
boundary, and preserves each request's original positions and true per-loop KV.

The example exposes intervals 1/2/4/8 and an eager same-readout reference. It keeps
full-depth prompt prefill, per-answer RNG, selected processed logprobs, raw tokens,
readout depths and stop/length reasons. Unread deep tails are discarded on stop.

Validation:

- 28 CPU tests

`parallel_compute_score_async` in `PrimeRewardManager` had no branch for dict results, so dict-returning reward functions (math_dapo, rlla, ...) hit `float(result[0])`, raised `KeyError: 0`, and `verify()`'s except-all fallback silently zeroed the whole batch.

This adds the same `isinstance(result, dict) -> result["score"]` handling that `NaiveRewardManager` / `BatchRewardManager` / `DAPORewardManager` already have.

## 背景

此 PR 添加了一个**跨仓库自动文档翻译工作流**（`schedule_doc_translate_ascend.yaml`），它能自动将 `docs/ascend_tutorial/zh/` 下的中文文档翻译为 `docs/ascend_tutorial/en/` 下的英文文档，并按周计划执行。


## 工作原理

此工作流在 `verl-project/verl` 仓库中运行，并使用**独立的私有 Fork 仓库**来存储翻译工具（Python 翻译引擎、技能/提示文档以及 `.po` 翻译记忆库）。这使得上游仓库保持整洁——它仅接收 `en/` 文档和工作流文件的更改。

### What does this PR do?

`ToolAgentLoop._call_tool` runs `create`, `execute` and `release` for every tool call. This PR creates the instance on the first call to a tool, reuses it for the rest of the trajectory, and releases every instance once when the trajectory ends, including when it raises.

`_wait_server_healthy()` calls `requests.get(.../health)` without a timeout. If the server accepts the connection but does not respond, startup polling blocks inside that request and cannot reach `is_process_alive()`.

items.title: fix(sglang): validate deployment config before launch
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.
items.body:
## Background

Multi-model SGLang configuration was resolved incrementally while deployment side effects were already being prepared. Invalid topology or ambiguous model entries could therefore fail late, after router or placement setup had begun.

## Problem

The config path did not validate whole-file invariants such as duplicate model names, multiple weight-updated models, complete engine topology, PP/TP consistency, or multi-node divisibility before launch.

## Solution

- Resolve every model and validate the complete config before placement or router startup.
- Reject unknown model fields

items.title: fix(sglang): bound local server startup waits
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.
items.body:
## Background

Locally managed SGLang servers are polled through `/health_generate` before rollout initialization can continue.

## Problem

The startup poll had neither a request timeout nor an overall deadline. A hung health request could block startup indefinitely, and failures while waiting left the newly spawned server process tree running.

## Solution

- Add `--sglang-server-startup-timeout` with a positive finite value and a conservative 600-second default.
- Use a monotonic deadline and cap every health request by both five seconds and the remaining startup budget.
- Reject readiness

## Background

A custom generation function may return multiple training segments for one input. `generate_and_rm_group` preserves that result as `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

When `group_rm` is enabled, the nested result was passed directly to the group reward function and trace helper. Those paths expect `list[Sample]`, so fan-out generation and group rewards could not be combined.

## Solution

- Flatten one level before tracing and invoking the group reward function.
- Assign returned rewards to the same leaves in stable fan-out order.

items.title: fix(rollout): handle nested aborted fully-async results
items.author: CharlesXu-HQ
items.summary: An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.
items.body:
## Background

`generate_and_rm_group` supports custom generation that fans one input out into `list[Sample]`, so a fully-async task can return `list[list[Sample]]`.

## Problem

The done callback inspected only the outer list. An aborted leaf inside a fan-out result could therefore enter the completed queue. Requeuing that nested output directly is also invalid because the next generation expects a flat input group.

## Solution

- Snapshot the flat input group before generation can mutate it.
- Inspect one-level fan-out leaves for `Sample.Status.ABORTED`.
- Requeue the pristine flat snapshot

items.body:
Fixes #2409

## Problem

`compute_gpqa_reward` falls back to a text match when no option letter can be extracted from the reply. That fallback (1) appended a one-letter gold label as answer text, and (2) searched each candidate as a raw substring of the normalized reply. A reply that never answers, for example `I'm sorry, but I can't help with that.`, therefore scored 1.0 whenever the gold letter (`a`, `b`, `c`) occurred inside a word, and a short numeric choice such as `11` matched inside `2011` or `111`.

## Approach

- A one-character label that is a valid option letter is no longer added t

## Summary

Fix CUDA autocast from downcasting the FP32 reduction used by VIME's fused PPO entropy path.

Under CUDA autocast, `torch.einsum` can run at a reduced precision even when both operands were explicitly promoted to FP32. The result is saved for entropy backward, so the precision loss affects both the reported entropy value and its gradient.

This change keeps only that CUDA reduction outside autocast and adds a one-GPU regression suite covering FP16/BF16 autocast, masked/unmasked log-prob paths, metric-only/gradient entropy, and chunked/non-chunked execution.

For example, total length 9 and response length 3 at CP=2 leave rank 0 with no response predictions, so indexing its last reward raises IndexError. If rank 0 owns earlier response predictions, the reward is instead attached to the wrong time step.

Use the existing CP token offsets to find the shard containing the final response token. CP=1 retains the existing behavior, and the per-token KL reward remains unchanged.

`distributed_masked_whiten(..., shift_mean=False)` used to center, scale, then add the mean back:

## Problem

Training and evaluation launch rollout tasks concurrently at three levels: samples within a rollout group, rollout groups within a training batch, and samples within an evaluation batch.

When one task raises an exception, the exception is propagated but the unfinished sibling tasks are not cancelled. They can continue generation or reward computation after the rollout has failed, wasting resources and potentially leaving unobserved task exceptions in the event loop.

## Fix

At each concurrency boundary, cancel unfinished sibling tasks and wait for their cleanup before re-raising

items.body:
Enabling KL (--kl-coef 0.1 or --use-kl-loss) without --ref-load used to die in slime_validate_args with `TypeError: _path_exists: path should be string, bytes, os.PathLike or integer, not NoneType`, because it stat'd args.ref_load before checking it was set. The sibling OPD check just below already guards for None first.

This adds the same guard: ref_load unset now raises a ValueError telling the user to pass --ref-load, and a ref_load that points nowhere still raises the original FileNotFoundError. Two unit tests cover both cases.

## Problem

Thanks to @kkyyxhll for catching in #2319 that SGLang ignores `sampling_params.temperature` when it computes input/prefill log-probs. OPD samples from the temperature-scaled student distribution `p_T`, so leaving the teacher at its implicit default computes `KL(p_T || q_1)`, not the matched-temperature objective `KL(p_T || q_T)`.

Passing the rollout temperature through sampling parameters is currently a no-op, while pinning it to `1.0` only makes the mismatched behavior explicit. Supporting the real-temperature case requires changing the SGLang input-logprob path.

items.summary: Fixes #2268 ## Problem runs a memory probe before every wrapped collective: calls /, which build the full dict — O(number of CUDA caching-allocator segments). Under the segment count grows across steps, so the probe gets progressively more expensive.
items.body:
Fixes #2268

## Problem

`slime/utils/reloadable_process_group.py::_wrap_low_level_call` runs a memory probe **before every wrapped collective**:

```python
def _wrap_low_level_call(check_memory=True):
    if check_memory:
        mem_info = available_memory()          # calls torch.cuda.memory_reserved()/allocated()
        if mem_info["free_GB"] < 3:
            clear_memory()
    yield
```

items.author: momo609
items.summary: Proposes online training of an external draft model during VIME RL training to maintain alignment with the evolving target model and sustain speculative decoding efficiency.
items.body:
# VIME External Draft Training Design

## 1. Background

VIME can already load an external EAGLE/DFlash/Dspark.. Draft model through vLLM's `SpeculativeConfig` for speculative decoding. However, online training currently only covers the MTP layers inside the Target model. As Target parameters change throughout RL training, an external Draft model gradually becomes misaligned. This lowers Draft-token acceptance and average acceptance length, and may
eventually make the additional Draft and verification cost larger than the speculative-decoding benefit.

items.body:
## Summary

Fix IPv6 URL construction in the vLLM engine control plane.

## Problem

The vLLM subprocess requires an unbracketed IPv6 address when binding
the server, while an IPv6 literal must be enclosed in brackets when
used as the host component of an HTTP URL.

Previously, the health-check path could construct an invalid URL such
as:

`http://2001:db8::1:8000/health`

instead of:

`http://[2001:db8::1]:8000/health`

The health check may then keep retrying failed requests, making engine
startup appear to be stuck.

items.body:
## Summary

This PR reduces actor-update memory usage when entropy is logged but does not contribute to the loss.

Long-context actor updates can become memory-bound because entropy is evaluated over the full vocabulary. When `entropy_coef == 0`, VIME still computes entropy metrics, but the entropy tensor is only used for reporting and has no gradient contribution. The current implementation always builds the entropy autograd graph and clones the full logits tensor before entropy computation, which increases peak memory without changing the loss.

This PR adds an optional rollout data transfer path for **disaggregated training** (separate rollout and actor GPUs). When enabled, vime transfers rollout tensors (`tokens`, `loss_masks`) through **Mooncake Store** instead of the Ray object store.

This is useful when rollout and training run on different GPUs or nodes and you want a dedicated high-bandwidth transfer layer rather than serializing large tensors through Ray.

Ported from [slime PR #1709](https://github.com/THUDM/slime/pull/1709).

items.body:
`abort()` ordered the worker calls as pause → drain → resume, which can hang the rollout under `--partial-rollout` with continuously-submitting (e.g. multi-turn) rollouts.

The call to `/pause?mode=abort` aborts the known requests but leaves the engine in`PAUSED_NEW` status, so a `/generate` POST that races in after the pause ends up in the waiting queue and never returns. One such request blocks the `while state.pendings` drain forever - and `/resume`, the only thing that frees it, sat after the drain.
